newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bank safety net deal signed - paper.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bank safety net deal signed - paper.

text.p: Argentina signed agreements with 13 foreign banks last Friday to set up a $5 billion safety net for banks, Central Bank president Pedro Pou said, quoted by a newspaper Wednesday.
Pou made the announcement in London, where he is accompanying Economy Minister Roque Fernandez on a trade mission, according to the Clarin newspaper.

Clarin did not say which banks signed the agreement, but the Central Bank said in August that it had received offers from institutions including the U.S. Chase Manhattan Bank and France's Societe Generale.

The privately-funded safety net will pay out funds to local banks in case of a run on deposits. It is being set up in response to the financial crisis which lashed Argentina at the start of last year and which caused several small banks to fail.
The Central Bank has also decided to start gradually increasing the minimum liquidity requirement for banks to 20 percent as of the first quarter of 1997, Pou said.
